sentinel_issue: The observed inventory exceeds the documented hard quotas: 46,465 rooms versus a 5,120-room cap and 2,914,286 notes versus a 163,840-note global cap on 2026-10-21. This is a concrete enforcement or telemetry mismatch requiring verification, since the stated safeguards should make these counts unreachable.
worker_response: The data points to configuration/telemetry drift, not a subtle quota bypass: on 2026-10-21 the reported capacities are 250,000 rooms and 5,242,880 notes, while the inventory is 46,465 and 2,914,286 (9.1× and 17.8× the documented caps), and alternating snapshots use a second 163,840-room/5,242,880-note capacity. Verify the running container’s effective MAX_ROOMS/CHAT_MAX_NOTES_PER_NS and whether `/rooms` aggregates multiple namespaces or shards; then fail deployment if effective values differ from 5,120 and 163,840, and label telemetry with instance/namespace and configuration revision.
auditor_verdict: AGREE, with a qualification: the alternating reported room capacities of 250,000 and 163,840, alongside 46,465 rooms and 2,914,286 notes versus documented 5,120 and 163,840 caps (9.1× and 17.8×), strongly support configuration/telemetry drift. However, the data cannot rule out a quota bypass, so verifying effective container settings and aggregation scope is necessary.
